reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Midlothian, Ellis County, Texas, whose exact power capacity Google does not publish. A third-party aggregator cites 86 MW for the campus, but this figure is unverified by Google itself and treated here as a lead rather than confirmed specification. Google's disclosure policy limits public information to aggregate state-level investment figures, withholding individual facility addresses, square footage, and power capacity.

If the 86 MW figure holds, the Midlothian campus would rank nineteenth among Texas facilities with any published capacity, and would represent roughly 18 percent of the 468 MW of capacity Texas operators have disclosed across 18 mapped sites. Texas hosts 133 mapped data center facilities overall, but only 18 operators publish power figures, so this campus's true rank and share depend on unpublished capacity at other sites. Google has announced plans to file for a fifth building at the Midlothian location as part of a broader $40 billion, three-AI-data-center Texas expansion, signaling continued investment in the region.

The absence of Google's own published power specification for this campus means its importance to AI scaling cannot be read from operator disclosure. The unconfirmed 86 MW lead suggests material scale, but verification would require either Google to publish the figure or independent measurement. The campus matters primarily as a marker of Google's multi-building commitment to Ellis County rather than as a quantified constraint on Texas or national AI infrastructure.
